assignmentFields: Government or civic location, if applicable

worldTravelerRules: Capital City: 21% of named NPCs may world travel.
City: 18% of named NPCs may world travel.
Town: 9% of named NPCs may world travel.
Village: 3% of named NPCs may world travel.
World map: show the NPC at their current resolved world location if NPC visibility is enabled.
Province map: show the NPC only if their current resolved location is inside that province.
Settlement map: show the NPC only if their current resolved location is inside that settlement.
If traveling between settlements, show the NPC at the current route segment, transit hub, or temporary travel marker.
If the NPC has not yet reached a destination, do not show them at the destination pin.
If the NPC has left a location, remove them from the old pin and update them to the new resolved location.

Generate GeoJSON from the settlement layout.
Generate districts, roads, paths, public spaces, buildings, rural zones, waterfront zones, and special regions.
Generate pinned locations from GeoJSON-backed features.
Apply settlement percentage targets to location categories.
Apply pin types and colors.
Generate named NPCs according to settlement type.
Generate NPC identity, relationships, residence needs, workplace needs, social role, schedule, alignment, plot hooks, and intrigue hooks.
Select world traveler NPCs according to settlement type percentage.
Assign residences.
Assign workplaces.
Assign civic, religious, commercial, educational, medical, criminal, noble, transportation, public, and special obligations.
Assign familial, romantic, professional, and personal visit locations.
Assign travel routes and temporary locations for world travelers.
Resolve current schedule location.
Attach NPCs to current pins.
Hide any NPCs that are still unassigned.
Display assigned NPCs on world, province, or settlement maps based on current time and current view.
Populate each pin panel with location and NPC data.
Save assignment data into the settlement model, GeoJSON properties, pin records, and NPC records.

pinsAndGeojson.finalBehaviorRequirement:
The final behavior should make the settlement feel alive and immersive.
NPCs are not just loose records in a directory. They are connected to actual GeoJSON-backed places in the settlement.
Each NPC has a home, workplace, schedule, relationships, social purpose, travel logic, and current location.
Each pin is not just a marker. It is a living simulation panel that contains location data, NPC data, relationship data, services, prices, hours, plot hooks, intrigue, government influence, religious influence, and economic information.
The map should show NPCs only where they currently belong according to the life simulator generator.

profiles.title: Capital City - Canyon Valley
profiles.overview: Prestigious, extravagant, exotic, heavily regulated, and expensive shopping, meals, housing, lodging, healing, crafting, transit, and repair services for a dark fantasy steampunk settlement.

locationProfile.biome_identity: cliff roads, rope bridges, switchback caravan yards, river-bottom markets, echo inns, gorge rail trestles, wind shelters, pulley lifts, and canyon rescue posts.
locationProfile.market_structure: grand bazaars, embassy hostels, luxury hotels, master guild courts, royal hospitals, relic vaults, and regulated portal offices. Elite purchases include tiny plated courses, rare materials, signed masterwork goods, and private appointments.
locationProfile.availability_rule: Capitals have the broadest stock, elite appointments, rare goods, and strict records for dangerous goods.
locationProfile.currency: 1 pp = 10 gp; 1 gp = 10 sp; 1 sp = 10 cp; 1 ep = 5 sp and is uncommon.
locationProfile.meal_portions_and_prices_intentionally_s: villages and towns serve larger practical portions, while cities and capitals add costly fine dining, tiny luxury courses, private rooms, rare ingredients, and formal service.

strictPlacementRules: Meal items are sold through hostels, taverns, inns, restaurants, hotels, tea houses, cafes, and market food stalls.
Bulk food is sold through general stores, granaries, grocers, and marketplaces.
Weapons, armor, ammunition, shields, and thundercoil gear are sold through armories, with repair and forged basics also handled by blacksmiths.

Craft goods are placed in specific craft shops: leatherworkers, tailors, textile shops, carpenters, furniture halls, potters, glassblowers, tinkers, locksmiths, wheelwrights, bowyers, chandlers, and artists.
Stables sell, rent, treat, and board mounts; wagonwrights and caravan yards handle carts, wagons, freight, and guards.

Potions, elixirs, licensed Cannabis remedies, poisons, antitoxins, acids, and alchemical goods are sold through apothecaries, herbalists, alchemists, clinics, hospitals, temple clinics, or licensed poison counters.
Mechanical, steam-driven, alchemical, and arcane-steam goods use designated craft, armory, alchemist, or guild counters.
